chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ja'far ibn 'Uthman, from Abu Basir, who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and a man said to him: May Allah perfect you. There are people in Kufa who say a statement that they attribute to you. He asked: What is it? He said: They say that faith (Iman) is not Islam. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Yes. The man said: Describe it to me. He said: Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah and acknowledges what has come from Allah, he is a Muslim. The man asked: And what is faith? He said: Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah and acknowledges what has come from Allah, establishes prayer, pays alms-tax, fasts the month of Ramadan, and performs pilgrimage to the House, and does not meet Allah with a sin for which Hellfire has been threatened, he is a believer. Abu Basir said: May I be your ransom, and which of us has not met Allah with a sin for which Hellfire has been threatened? He said: It is not where you think. It is only he who has not met Allah with a sin for which Hellfire has been threatened and has not repented from it.

key_terms.أَوْعَدَ عَلَيْهِ النَّارَ: For which Hellfire has been threatened/promised

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Islam and Iman in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction between Islam (outward submission) and Iman (inner faith with ritual practice) is clarified to address the claims of the Kufans who conflated the two. The Imam defines Iman as Islam augmented by the performance of pillars and the absence of unrepented major sins, a definition that underscores the Shia emphasis on the integration of belief and action. This hadith is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the minimal requirements of being a Muslim and the fuller state of being a believer with guaranteed salvation.

en.basel-kadem: 9.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said:

We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim bin Hashim, from his father, from al-Nawfaly, from al-Sukuni, from Abu Abdillah, from his fathers, peace be upon them, that he said: Indeed, it is among humbleness that a man is pleased with one sitting place before more sitting places, that he sends peace upon the one he meets, that he abandons quarreling, even if he is rightful, and that he does not like to be praised for godfearness.
